mitigations.name: Limit Public Release of Information
mitigations.description: Limit the public release of technical information about the AI stack used in an organization's products or services.

mitigations.name: Limit Model Artifact Release
mitigations.description: Limit public release of technical project details including data, algorithms, model architectures, and model checkpoints that are used in production, or that are representative of those used in production.

mitigations.name: Passive AI Output Obfuscation
mitigations.description: Decreasing the fidelity of model outputs provided to the end user can reduce an adversary's ability to extract information about the model and optimize attacks for the model.

mitigations.name: Model Hardening
mitigations.description: Use techniques to make AI models robust to adversarial inputs such as adversarial training or network distillation.

mitigations.name: Restrict Number of AI Model Queries
mitigations.description: Limit the total number and rate of queries a user can perform.

mitigations.name: Control Access to AI Models and Data at Rest
mitigations.description: Establish access controls on internal model registries and limit internal access to production models. Limit access to training data only to approved users.

mitigations.name: Use Ensemble Methods
mitigations.description: Use an ensemble of models for inference to increase robustness to adversarial inputs. Some attacks may effectively evade one model or model family but be ineffective against others.

mitigations.name: Sanitize Training Data
mitigations.description: Detect and remove or remediate poisoned training data. Training data should be sanitized prior to model training and recurrently for an active learning model.

mitigations.name: Validate AI Model
mitigations.description: Validate that AI models perform as intended by testing for backdoor triggers, potential for data leakage, or adversarial influence.

mitigations.name: Use Multi-Modal Sensors
mitigations.description: Incorporate multiple sensors to integrate varying perspectives and modalities to avoid a single point of failure susceptible to physical attacks.

mitigations.name: Input Restoration
mitigations.description: Preprocess all inference data to nullify or reverse potential adversarial perturbations.

mitigations.name: Restrict Library Loading
mitigations.description: Prevent abuse of library loading mechanisms in the operating system and software to load untrusted code by configuring appropriate library loading mechanisms and investigating potential vulnerable software.

mitigations.name: Encrypt Sensitive Information
mitigations.description: Encrypt sensitive data such as AI models to protect against adversaries attempting to access sensitive data.

mitigations.name: Code Signing
mitigations.description: Enforce binary and application integrity with digital signature verification to prevent untrusted code from executing. Adversaries can embed malicious code in AI software or models.

mitigations.name: Verify AI Artifacts
mitigations.description: Verify the cryptographic checksum of all AI artifacts to verify that the file was not modified by an attacker.

mitigations.name: Adversarial Input Detection
mitigations.description: Detect and block adversarial inputs or atypical queries that deviate from known benign behavior, exhibit behavior patterns observed in previous attacks or that come from potentially malicious IPs.

mitigations.name: Vulnerability Scanning
mitigations.description: Vulnerability scanning is used to find potentially exploitable software vulnerabilities to remediate them.

mitigations.name: AI Model Distribution Methods
mitigations.description: Deploying AI models to edge devices can increase the attack surface of the system. Consider serving models in the cloud to reduce the level of access the adversary has to the model.

mitigations.name: User Training
mitigations.description: Educate AI model developers to on AI supply chain risks and potentially malicious AI artifacts. Educate users on how to identify deepfakes and phishing attempts.

mitigations.name: Control Access to AI Models and Data in Production
mitigations.description: Require users to verify their identities before accessing a production model. Require authentication for API endpoints and monitor production model queries to ensure compliance with usage policies and to prevent model...

mitigations.name: Generative AI Guardrails
mitigations.description: Guardrails are safety controls that are placed between a generative AI model and the output shared with the user to prevent undesired inputs and outputs.

mitigations.name: Generative AI Guidelines
mitigations.description: Guidelines are safety controls that are placed between user-provided input and a generative AI model to help direct the model to produce desired outputs and prevent undesired outputs.

mitigations.name: Generative AI Model Alignment
mitigations.description: When training or fine-tuning a generative AI model it is important to utilize techniques that improve model alignment with safety, security, and content policies.

mitigations.name: AI Bill of Materials
mitigations.description: An AI Bill of Materials (AI BOM) contains a full listing of artifacts and resources that were used in building the AI.

mitigations.name: AI Telemetry Logging
mitigations.description: Implement logging of inputs and outputs of deployed AI models. When deploying AI agents, implement logging of the intermediate steps of agentic actions and decisions, data access and tool use, installation commands, and...

mitigations.name: Maintain AI Dataset Provenance
mitigations.description: Maintain a detailed history of datasets used for AI applications. The history should include information about the dataset's source as well as a complete record of any modifications.

mitigations.name: Privileged AI Agent Permissions Configuration
mitigations.description: AI agents may be granted elevated privileges above that of a normal user to enable desired workflows. When deploying a privileged AI agent, or an agent that interacts with multiple users, it is important to implement...

mitigations.name: Single-User AI Agent Permissions Configuration
mitigations.description: When deploying an AI agent that acts as a representative of a user and performs actions on their behalf, it is important to implement robust policies and controls on permissions and lifecycle management of the agent.

mitigations.name: AI Agent Tools Permissions Configuration
mitigations.description: When deploying tools that will be shared across multiple AI agents, it is important to implement robust policies and controls on permissions for the tools.

mitigations.name: Human In-the-Loop for AI Agent Actions
mitigations.description: Systems should require the user or another human stakeholder to approve AI agent actions before the agent takes them. The human approver may be technical staff or business unit SMEs depending on the use case.

mitigations.name: Restrict AI Agent Tool Invocation on Untrusted Data
mitigations.description: Untrusted data can contain prompt injections that invoke an AI agent's tools, potentially causing confidentiality, integrity or availability violations.

mitigations.name: Memory Hardening
mitigations.description: Memory Hardening involves developing trust boundaries and secure processes for how an AI agent stores and accesses memory and context.

mitigations.name: Segmentation of AI Agent Components
mitigations.description: Define security boundaries around agentic tools and data sources with methods such as API access, container isolation, code execution sandboxing, and rate limiting of tool invocation.

mitigations.name: Input and Output Validation for AI Agent Components
mitigations.description: Implement validation on inputs and outputs for the tools and data sources used by AI agents. Validation includes enforcing a common data format, schema validation, checks for sensitive or prohibited information leakage,...

mitigations.name: Deepfake Detection
mitigations.description: Apply deepfake detection algorithms against any untrusted or user-provided data, especially in impactful applications such as biometric verification, to block generated content.
